records.title: G05/F95 Transfer-Case Shudder: Tires and Fluid Diagnosis First
records.description: On G05 X5 and F95 X5 M vehicles with the ATX13-X transfer case, a low-speed shudder or jerking while cornering or accelerating can be caused by mismatched, incorrectly fitted, or unevenly worn tires, or by transfer-case oil that does not meet BMW specifications. BMW's bulletin describes this complaint without warning lights or Check Control messages. That symptom is not evidence that a universal actuator motor failed, and part 27-10-7-643-751 is a complete older E70 xDrive35i transfer box—not an actuator for these vehicles.
records.solution: Follow BMW SIB 27 02 20 in order: verify all four tires for VIN-correct size, brand/application, axle placement, and wear; diagnose any powertrain faults; then use ISTA to temporarily deactivate the transfer-case clutch and road-test the complaint. Only if the shudder disappears with the VTG deactivated does BMW direct an ATX13-X oil change with DTF-1, followed by VTG calibration. The clutch plates can require up to 125 miles after the service to become fully saturated and smooth out. If the symptom remains, continue diagnosis rather than buying an actuator or transfer case. Part numbers for any further repair must be selected by VIN in ETK/AIR.
symptoms: Clicking or grinding from under center console area

citations.description: BMW SIB 27 02 20 ATX13-X transfer-case shudder diagnosis and fluid procedure

communityRecommendations.content: Before servicing the transfer case, compare all four tires for correct size, approved application, axle placement, and similar wear; tire mismatch can keep xDrive engaged and create the shudder.
Do not buy an actuator from the shudder alone. BMW first isolates the transfer case with ISTA, then changes and calibrates the fluid only if that test removes the complaint.

fixParts.note: BMW's ATX13-X procedure uses approximately 0.7 liter from a 1-liter container, then requires VTG calibration and up to 125 miles of run-in. Confirm the current fluid number by VIN/ETK before ordering.

variants.note: DTF-1 service material specified by BMW SIB 27 02 20; not an automatic repair for warning lights or other driveline faults.
variants.scope: G05 X5 / F95 X5 M with ATX13-X after tire and ISTA isolation checks

fixParts.component: BMW DTF-1 transfer-case oil, 1 liter (only after SIB 27 02 20 diagnosis selects oil service)

records.title: VANOS Adjustment-Unit Bolt Recall and Cam-Timing Faults (Inline-Six)
records.description: Certain model-year 2010-2013 E70 X5 vehicles with an N52-family or N55 inline-six engine are included in BMW/NHTSA safety recall 23V-707. Aluminum fasteners in the intake and exhaust VANOS adjustment units can loosen or break, causing incorrect camshaft adjustment, unusual engine noise, rough running, a check-engine warning, reduced-power mode, a no-start condition, or, rarely, an engine stall. These symptoms and VANOS/camshaft faults do not by themselves prove that replaceable control solenoid 11-36-7-585-425 has failed, and the recall does not apply to every X5 engine or model year.
records.solution: Enter the VIN in BMW's official recall lookup and have an authorized BMW center complete recall 23V-707 if it is open. BMW's procedure is inspection-dependent: intact affected bolts are replaced; if bolts are loose or broken, the affected VANOS adjustment unit is replaced, and missing fragments must be recovered. The recall repair is free, so do not buy a solenoid or VANOS part first. If the VIN is outside the recall or a fault remains after the remedy, use BMW-capable diagnostics to test oil supply and pressure, wiring, sensors, control solenoids, adjustment units, and mechanical timing before selecting a part. If the engine runs roughly, makes unusual mechanical noise, loses power, or stalls, move out of traffic safely, stop driving, and contact BMW for transport guidance.
symptoms: Rough idle or engine misfires (especially at low RPM)
Sluggish acceleration and loss of power
Check engine light with codes 2A82, 2A87, 2A88 (VANOS solenoid codes)
Loud ticking or rattling from engine

citations.description: BMW SIB 11 09 23 recall scope, condition, and inspection-dependent repair
BMW/NHTSA 23V-707 owner notice and safety instructions

communityRecommendations.content: Check the VIN for recall 23V-707 before paying for VANOS diagnosis or parts; BMW performs an open recall remedy free of charge.
A VANOS or camshaft fault is not proof of a failed solenoid. The recall remedy depends on the bolt inspection, and non-recall faults require BMW-capable diagnosis before any part is ordered.

fixParts.note: Recall-first information only. Do not buy a retail solenoid or bolt kit; an authorized BMW center checks the VIN and performs the inspection-dependent 23V-707 remedy free of charge.

records.title: E70 xDrive35i N55 Electric Coolant Pump (Fault-Confirmed)
records.description: The 2011-2013 E70 X5 xDrive35i uses an electronically controlled N55 engine-coolant pump. A temperature warning, reduced-power message, fan running at high speed, or cooling-system fault can involve the pump, but low coolant, a leak, wiring or ground, power supply, thermostat, temperature sensing, trapped air, or another cooling fault can produce overlapping symptoms. Current BMW pump 11-51-5-A05-704 is cataloged for the N55 E70 application; it is not the common pump for the N52 xDrive30i, N63 xDrive50i, or every F15 X5, and the thermostat is a separate VIN-selected component.
records.solution: If the engine-temperature warning appears, stop safely, shut the engine off, and tow the vehicle if normal temperature cannot be confirmed. When cool, check coolant level and leaks, read BMW-specific faults, verify pump power/ground and communication, and run the ISTA coolant-pump activation/test plan. If those tests confirm the pump and BMW ETK/AIR selects 11-51-5-A05-704 for the VIN, replace it using the BMW procedure, select the thermostat separately only if testing or preventive planning justifies it, vacuum-fill or bleed the system as specified, and verify commanded pump operation and stable temperature. Do not use a fixed-mileage rule or this part number for an N52, N63, or F15 without VIN confirmation.
symptoms: Coolant leaking near front of engine
Engine temperature drops when accelerating (pump volume failure)
Coolant warning light or "Engine Overheating" message
Check engine light with cooling system codes

citations.description: Official BMW 11515A05704 electric coolant-pump identity and engine applications
BMW electric coolant-pump part and 2011-2013 X5 fitment

communityRecommendations.content: If an overheat warning appears, stop safely and shut the engine off; continued operation can cause major engine damage. Tow it if normal temperature cannot be verified.
Ask for the BMW pump activation result plus power, ground, leak, and thermostat checks before approving the pump.

fixParts.note: Current N54/N55 electric pump for the cataloged 2011-2013 E70 xDrive35i application. The thermostat is separate; confirm both components by VIN before ordering.
